subject: SCIENCE
title: Plant Parts and Jobs
objective: Identify common plant parts and functions while recognizing variation.
introduction: Roots, stems, leaves, and flowers — every part of a plant has a job. Can you match each part to its job?

vocabulary.definition: A living thing that grows in soil and makes food.
The part of a plant that holds it in the soil.
The part of a plant that carries water up.

items.prompt: Which statement about plant parts is true?

options.text: Many flowering plants have roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds, but not every plant has every part at every stage.

items.explanation: Most flowering plants have roots, stems, leaves, and more, but plants differ — not every plant has every part all the time. Soil is not plant food, and not every plant flowers.

items.prompt: Which pair matches a plant part to its job?

options.text: leaves hold the plant in the soil

items.explanation: Roots soak up water and hold the plant in place. Leaves make food, and stems carry water up — they do not do roots' jobs.

items.prompt: Which statement is not true?  (in this lesson: Plant Parts and Jobs)
items.explanation: Plants make their own food in their leaves using light. Soil holds water and nutrients, but it is not food.

items.prompt: Which part often anchors a plant?
items.explanation: Roots grow into the soil and hold the plant in place. Flowers and fruits do not anchor the plant.

items.prompt: Which plant part goes with the right job?

options.text: flowers soak up water from soil

items.explanation: Leaves make food for the plant using light. Roots take in water and hold the plant, and flowers make seeds.
